newsitem.title: USA: One year after stepping down, Dole visits Senate.
newsitem.headline: One year after stepping down, Dole visits Senate.

text.p: One year after stepping down as Senate leader to devote his time to a presidential bid that failed, Bob Dole returned for lunch with his former Republican colleagues Tuesday.

Now a Washington lawyer who makes an occasional lucrative commercial on the side, Dole joined Republicans for their weekly policy luncheon and brought a cake for Sen. Strom Thurmond, the 94-year-old South Carolinian who last month set a record as the longest-serving senator.

Dole left the Senate last June 11 to devote himself fulltime to campaign against President Clinton. Greeted warmly by colleagues and tourists who rushed to pose with him as he passed through familiar corriders, Dole said he was doing fine in private life although his dog Leader was beginning to show his age.
"He's hard of hearing and sleeps all day," Dole joked.
Dole said he had just taken a prospective client out to lunch for the first time at a posh Washington restaurant and discovered, "Boy, that's expensive."
